attributes.decisive_finding: The third cluster is a SYMBOL-ATTRIBUTION difference, not register noise, and it is TU-wide rather than local to this function. Our critter.c declares `extern u64 gControllerButtons` (line 585) as one 8-byte object, so a 64-bit AND emits its low half as the relocation `gControllerButtons+0x4`. config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt however defines TWO adjacent 4-byte objects - gControllerButtons at 0x803445C8 and sFlags at 0x803445CC - so the target's disassembly symbolises the identical address as `sFlags`. Same address, same linked bytes, different spelling. See the accompanying law record for the project-level consequence.

attributes.residual: real 22-24 = three named mechanisms. (1) An f0/f1 FPR crossing in the Effects scale block: target loads the 188(r4) operand into f0 and 8(r30) into f1, ours does the reverse, carrying through the two following fmuls and the stfs. (2) An r6/r7 GPR crossing in the node-index block: target puts the `lha 70(r30)` result in r6 and the `r4+8` base in r7, ours reverses both, carrying through extsh./lwzx/mulli. Both are pure disjoint recolors with IDENTICAL opcode streams and are WEBFRANK-READY under copy_register_fields. (3) The gControllerButtons/sFlags relocation spelling, 2 lines, NOT source-reachable from this TU - see the law record.
